# Results — Study 91 (Death-Cross) on the real total-return tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — hold SPY while
the **SMA(50) ≥ SMA(200)**, sit in cash (earning **0%**) otherwise, act one day after the
cross (signal at close *t* → position at *t+1*), charge **5 bps** per switch — run on the
**total-return** SPY tape and pinned against (a) buy-and-hold and (b) a **matched
random-timing control** that holds the same total time in cash, in runs of the same
lengths, at random dates. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold
the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY (total return) | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | `eb1569cc9e97` |

## The honest test — net of 5 bps/switch

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Time in mkt | Switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Death-cross timer** | **9.64%** | 13.7% | **0.743** | **−33.7%** | 75% | 31 |
| Buy & hold | 10.82% | 18.6% | 0.646 | −55.2% | 100% | 0 |
| Random-timing coin (matched, 200 seeds) | 8.05% | — | 0.564 | −51.0% | 75% | — |

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Timer Sharpe − buy-and-hold Sharpe | **+0.097** |
| Does it beat the matched random coin? | **195 / 200 seeds (98%)** on Sharpe |
| HAC *t* on the daily return difference (timer − buy-and-hold) | **−0.99** |
| Drawdown cut vs buy-and-hold | **+21.5 pts** (−33.7% vs −55.2%) |
| CAGR vs buy-and-hold | **−1.18 pts/yr** (9.64% vs 10.82%) |

## How to read it

- **The crashes are really dodged** — drawdown falls from −55% to −34% and volatility from
  19% to 14%, and the timer beats an exposure-matched random coin 98% of the time. The
  *dates* carry information; this is not just "be in cash sometimes." → 3rd axis
  **CONFIRMED**.
- **But it does not beat buy-and-hold.** It earns **1.2 pts/yr less** (9.64% vs 10.82%),
  and the Sharpe edge (+0.097) does not clear the bar: HAC *t* on the excess return is
  **−0.99**. The improvement is lower equity exposure — i.e. **less beta** — which a
  risk-averse investor could buy more cheaply by simply holding less SPY. → Signal
  **WEAK**, Tradability **MIRAGE** for the "beat the market" claim.
